# Left Operand

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:LeftOperand`](gmeow-LeftOperand.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/LeftOperand>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/rights`](../../slices/rights.md)
- **Box roles:** [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The dimension an atomic constraint tests — an OPEN value vocabulary mirroring the ODRL [`leftOperand`](../properties/gmeow-leftOperand.md) vocabulary (dateTime, spatial, count, purpose, recipient, industry, …).

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:LeftOperand`](gmeow-LeftOperand.md) as a specialized kind of [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use as the open value vocabulary for the constraint-dimension axis — the operand (dateTime, spatial, count, purpose, recipient, …) an atomic constraint tests, referenced via [`gmeow:leftOperand`](../properties/gmeow-leftOperand.md).

### Avoid when

- Avoid minting per-dimension subclasses (operands are individuals, [Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)) and avoid inventing a free-text dimension; reuse a seeded ODRL value or mint a fresh individual.

### How to use

- Reference a seeded value ([`gmeow:leftOpDateTime`](../individuals/gmeow-leftOpDateTime.md), [`gmeow:leftOpSpatial`](../individuals/gmeow-leftOpSpatial.md), …) from [`gmeow:leftOperand`](../properties/gmeow-leftOperand.md); mint a new individual aligned to ODRL by reference when a needed dimension is missing.

### Examples

- ex:opPurpose a [`gmeow:LeftOperand`](gmeow-LeftOperand.md); [rdfs:label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "purpose"@en.
